title: Passat simple: parlà, perdé, dormí
summary: The literary past tense: the endings of the three conjugations and the irregular verbs.
explanation:
The passat simple (parlà, perdé, dormí) means the same as the passat perifràstic (va parlar, unit 59): a finished action in the past. It is one tense written in two ways:

passat perifràsticpassat simple
jovaig parlarparlí
tuvas parlarparlares
ell, ellava parlarparlà
nosaltresvam parlarparlàrem
vosaltresvau parlarparlàreu
ells, ellesvan parlarparlaren

In everyday speech in Catalonia people say vaig parlar. Parlà is found in books, news and formal writing, mostly in the 3rd person (digué, arribaren, fou), and Valencian speakers use it in conversation too. So it is enough to recognise these forms when you read; you don’t have to use them yourself.

Endings

Add the ending to the stem (the infinitive without -ar, -re, -er, -ir). The second conjugation is the same for verbs in -re (2a) and in -er (2b).

1 (-ar): cantar2a (-re): perdre2b (-er): témer3 (-ir): dormir
jocantíperdítemídormí
tucantaresperderestemeresdormires
ell, ellacantàperdétemédormí
nosaltrescantàremperdéremteméremdormírem
vosaltrescantàreuperdéreuteméreudormíreu
ells, ellescantarenperderentemerendormiren
  • The stress always falls on the ending, so it carries an accent: parlà, perdé, dormí; parlàrem, perdéreu.
  • In the third conjugation the jo and ell forms are the same: dormí means both “I slept” and “he slept”.
  • -ir verbs that take -eix- (servir, servEIXo) do not take it here: serví, servires, serví…

Spelling changes

Before the -í of the first person the stem keeps its sound, so the spelling changes:

joell, ella
tocartoquítocà
pagarpaguípagà
començarcomencícomençà
menjarmengímenjà

Irregular verbs

serferestartenirdirveure
jofuifiuestiguítinguídiguíviu

Anar and saber are regular here: aní, anares, anà…; sabí, saberes, sabé…

Stems in -gu-, -qu-

If the past participle ends in -gut (pogut, begut), the passat simple stem has -gu-; if it ends in -scut (viscut, nascut), -squ-. The endings are those of the second conjugation: poguí, pogueres, pogué, poguérem, poguéreu, pogueren.

* Prendre (pres) and dur (dut) also take -gu-, though their participle gives no hint. So do their compounds: aprendre → aprenguí, comprendre → comprenguí.

examples.en: They arrived in Barcelona at dawn.
It was a very hot summer.
That night he didn’t sleep at all.
We were lucky and found a seat.
